title: A reciprocal function on a neighbourhood of a finite affine complement
statement: Let $X$ be an integral [def-pc-integral-scheme], separated [def-weil-proper-morphism], locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme] scheme [def-pc-scheme] of topological Krull dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Let $U$ be a nonempty affine open with finite complement. There exist an open $V$, $f\in\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $g\in\mathcal O_X(V)$ such that $U\cup V=X$, the restrictions of $f$ and $g$ to $U\cap V$ multiply to $1$, and $D(g)=U\cap V$, where $D(g)$ denotes the points of $V$ at which the germ of $g$ is a unit in the local ring.

source.place: Varieties Lemma 09NB (varieties-lemma-find-globally-generated), proof, first paragraph and the open covering

proof.text: For every x outside U, its stalk is a Noetherian local domain with fraction field k(X). Its dimension is at most one by the generalization-chain description; the generic point lies in the nonempty U and strictly generalizes x, giving dimension at least one. The affine ring O(U) also has fraction field k(X). Separatedness gives the surjectivity of O(U) tensor O_{X,x} -> k(X).

Apply the common-denominator theorem to the finite family of local stalks. Local rings are semilocal and their Jacobson radical is their maximal ideal. Obtain nonzero f in O(U) whose inverse has a representative b_x in each maximal ideal.

Represent each b_x on a neighbourhood V_x of x. Representatives agree on overlaps: their images in k(X) are the same inverse of f, and sections on nonempty opens inject into k(X); empty overlaps have unique sections. Glue them by the structure-sheaf axiom to g on V = union V_x. Then U union V = X. On U intersect V, fg = 1 by the same injectivity. Thus g is a unit there, while at each x outside U its germ is b_x in the maximal ideal. Hence D(g) = U intersect V. If the complement is empty, take V empty and f = 1.
